rules.title: Your cache folder (~/.cache)
rules.summary: Per-user caches of apps (XDG cache); safe to clear, apps rebuild them
rules.whatItIs: The XDG cache directory where desktop apps and tools keep non-essential cached data: browser caches, thumbnails, pip, shader caches and more.
rules.whyBig: Browsers, package managers and shader caches grow without limit in many apps; several GB is common.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing important is lost; apps rebuild their caches. A few tools also keep downloaded models or login tokens here (for example Hugging Face), which then need downloading or signing in again.
rules.saferAlternative: Delete the largest subfolders while the owning apps are closed.

rules.title: Thumbnail cache
rules.summary: File manager thumbnails; rebuilt automatically
rules.whatItIs: Thumbnails that file managers (Nautilus, Dolphin, Thunar) create for pictures, videos and documents.
rules.whyBig: Every previewed file adds thumbnails in several sizes, and thumbnails of deleted files stay.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; thumbnails are recreated when folders are opened.

rules.title: pip cache
rules.summary: Downloaded and built Python packages; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: pip's HTTP cache and locally built wheels.
rules.whyBig: Large packages (PyTorch, CUDA libraries) are cached at full size.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; packages are downloaded again.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'pip cache purge'.

rules.title: Mesa shader cache
rules.summary: Compiled GPU shaders of the Mesa drivers; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Shaders compiled by Mesa's open-source graphics drivers (AMD, Intel) for games and apps.
rules.whyBig: Each game adds compiled shaders up to Mesa's cache size limit.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; games recompile shaders and may stutter at first.

rules.title: Mesa shader cache (database)
rules.summary: Compiled GPU shaders of newer Mesa drivers; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Newer Mesa versions keep the shader cache in this database-style folder.
rules.whyBig: Each game adds compiled shaders up to the cache size limit.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; games recompile shaders and may stutter at first.

rules.title: NVIDIA shader cache
rules.summary: Compiled shaders of the NVIDIA driver; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Shader caches (GLCache) of the proprietary NVIDIA driver.
rules.whyBig: Each game adds compiled shaders.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; shaders are recompiled with some stutter at first.

rules.title: Playwright browsers
rules.summary: Browsers downloaded by Playwright; re-download with playwright install
rules.whatItIs: Browser builds Playwright downloads to run automation and tests.
rules.whyBig: Each Playwright version downloads its own builds without removing old ones.
rules.ifDeleted: Playwright fails until 'npx playwright install' runs again.

rules.title: Trash
rules.summary: Files you moved to the trash; empty it after checking
rules.whatItIs: The desktop trash (freedesktop.org standard): deleted files (files) and their original locations (info).
rules.whyBig: Deleted files keep their full size until the trash is emptied.
rules.ifDeleted: The files can no longer be restored.
rules.saferAlternative: Open the trash in your file manager, restore what you need and choose Empty Trash.

rules.title: Steam
rules.summary: Steam client, its default library (steamapps) and shader caches
rules.whatItIs: The Steam client's home on Linux, with its default library: games, Proton prefixes (compatdata), shader caches and Workshop content.
rules.whyBig: Installed games are the bulk; Proton and shader caches add many GB.
rules.ifDeleted: Steam and every game in this library stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall games from Steam or move them in Settings > Storage.

rules.title: Godot editor data
rules.summary: Godot export templates and the user data of your projects and games
rules.whatItIs: Godot's data folder: export templates and the user:// data of your projects and games (app_userdata).
rules.whyBig: Export templates are about 1 GB per Godot version.
rules.ifDeleted: Export templates and project save data are lost.

rules.title: Godot export templates
rules.summary: Export templates per Godot version; downloaded again from the editor
rules.whatItIs: Templates the Godot editor uses to export games, one folder per version.
rules.whyBig: About 1 GB per version; old ones stay after upgrading.
rules.ifDeleted: Exporting fails until templates are downloaded again.

rules.title: Godot project and game user data
rules.summary: user:// data of your Godot projects and games, including saves
rules.whatItIs: The user:// folders of Godot projects and games.
rules.whyBig: Usually small; logs and caches can grow.
rules.ifDeleted: Saves and settings of those projects and games are lost.

rules.title: Podman containers and images
rules.summary: Rootless Podman images, containers and volumes; prune, do not delete
rules.whatItIs: Storage of rootless Podman (and Buildah): images, container layers and volumes.
rules.whyBig: Every pulled image, build layer and volume.
rules.ifDeleted: All containers, images and volume data are lost, and Podman's storage state may need a reset.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'podman system prune' (add -a for unused images).

rules.title: Flatpak apps (per user)
rules.summary: Flatpak apps and runtimes installed for your user
rules.whatItIs: Apps and runtimes installed with 'flatpak install --user'.
rules.whyBig: Each runtime is hundreds of MB, and unused runtimes stay after apps are removed.
rules.ifDeleted: Those Flatpak apps stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'flatpak uninstall --unused' to remove unused runtimes.

rules.title: Flatpak app data
rules.summary: Per-app data, config and caches of your Flatpak apps
rules.whatItIs: Each Flatpak app keeps its own config, data and cache here (one folder per app ID).
rules.whyBig: Browsers, Steam and messengers installed as Flatpaks keep their whole profile and cache here.
rules.ifDeleted: The apps lose their settings and data; caches are rebuilt.
rules.saferAlternative: Delete only the cache subfolders, or folders of apps you have uninstalled.

rules.title: Flatpak app cache
rules.summary: Cache of a Flatpak app; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: The XDG cache folder of one Flatpak app.
rules.whyBig: Browsers and media apps cache a lot.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing important is lost; the app rebuilds it. Close the app first.

rules.title: Snap app data
rules.summary: Per-user data of Snap apps, one folder per app and revision
rules.whatItIs: Snap apps keep your data for each app here, with folders per revision plus a 'common' folder.
rules.whyBig: Browsers and IDEs installed as snaps keep their profiles and caches here.
rules.ifDeleted: The apps lose their settings and data.

rules.title: Home folders
rules.summary: Home folders of the users on this system
rules.whatItIs: Each subfolder is one user's home with their files, settings (dot-folders) and caches.
rules.whyBig: Personal files plus app data and caches.
rules.ifDeleted: Users lose their files and settings.

rules.title: Your home folder
rules.summary: Your home folder: personal files plus app settings and caches
rules.whatItIs: Your home directory. Hidden dot-folders hold settings (~/.config), data (~/.local/share) and caches (~/.cache).
rules.whyBig: Personal files plus app data and caches.
rules.ifDeleted: Your files and settings are gone.

rules.title: APT package cache
rules.summary: Downloaded .deb packages; clear with apt clean
rules.whatItIs: Package files APT downloaded to install or upgrade software.
rules.whyBig: Old package versions accumulate unless apt cleans them.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; packages are downloaded again when needed.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'sudo apt clean' (or 'sudo apt autoclean' to keep current versions).

rules.title: APT package lists
rules.summary: Package index files; recreated by apt update
rules.whatItIs: Package lists downloaded by 'apt update'.
rules.whyBig: Usually a few hundred MB.
rules.ifDeleted: apt cannot install anything until you run 'sudo apt update' again.

rules.title: DNF package cache
rules.summary: Package metadata and downloads of DNF; clear with dnf clean all
rules.whatItIs: Metadata and packages cached by DNF on Fedora and related distributions.
rules.whyBig: Metadata for every repository and any kept packages.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; DNF downloads metadata again.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'sudo dnf clean all'.

rules.title: pacman package cache
rules.summary: Downloaded Arch packages kept for downgrades; trim with paccache
rules.whatItIs: Every package version pacman downloaded; Arch keeps them all so you can downgrade.
rules.whyBig: It grows with every system update and can reach many GB.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks, but you can no longer downgrade to cached versions offline.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'paccache -r' (pacman-contrib) to keep the last three versions.

rules.title: System caches (/var/cache)
rules.summary: Caches of system services and package managers
rules.whatItIs: Cached data of system programs: package managers, font caches, man page indexes and services.
rules.whyBig: Package manager caches are the usual large part.
rules.ifDeleted: Most caches are rebuilt, but deleting the whole folder can disturb running services; use the package manager's clean command instead.

rules.title: System logs
rules.summary: System and service logs; rotated logs can go, active logs should stay
rules.whatItIs: Logs of the system and services, including rotated archives (.1, .gz) and the systemd journal.
rules.whyBig: Chatty services, a crash loop or a disabled log rotation can fill it quickly.
rules.ifDeleted: Deleting active log files confuses the services writing them; rotated archives can go.
rules.saferAlternative: Delete old *.gz and *.1 files, and shrink the journal with journalctl.

rules.title: systemd journal
rules.summary: Persistent systemd journal; shrink it with journalctl --vacuum-size
rules.whatItIs: The systemd journal's persistent log files.
rules.whyBig: By default it may use up to 10% of the file system (capped at 4 GB).
rules.ifDeleted: Deleting files by hand while journald runs can corrupt the journal; you lose log history.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'sudo journalctl --vacuum-size=500M', and set SystemMaxUse in journald.conf to keep it small.

rules.title: Core dumps (systemd)
rules.summary: Crash dumps of programs; safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: Compressed core dumps that systemd-coredump saves when a program crashes.
rules.whyBig: Each dump holds the crashed program's memory; repeated crashes add up.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; those crashes can no longer be debugged.

rules.title: Crash reports (apport)
rules.summary: Crash reports of Ubuntu's apport; safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: Crash reports and dumps collected by apport on Ubuntu.
rules.whyBig: Each report can contain a full core dump.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; unsent reports are not sent.

rules.title: Docker data
rules.summary: Docker images, containers, volumes and build cache; prune, never delete
rules.whatItIs: Docker's data root: image layers (overlay2), containers, volumes and build cache.
rules.whyBig: Every pulled image, stopped container, unused volume and build cache layer stays until pruned.
rules.ifDeleted: Docker's state is corrupted and all containers, images and volumes (including databases stored in volumes) are lost.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'docker system prune' (add -a for all unused images; add --volumes only if no volume holds data you need).

rules.title: containerd data
rules.summary: Image and container storage of containerd; manage it with its tools
rules.whatItIs: Storage of containerd, used by Docker and Kubernetes: image content and snapshots.
rules.whyBig: Every pulled image and snapshot.
rules.ifDeleted: Container runtimes break and images are lost.
rules.saferAlternative: Prune through Docker ('docker system prune') or your Kubernetes tools.

rules.title: Flatpak apps and runtimes
rules.summary: System-wide Flatpak apps and runtimes; remove unused runtimes with flatpak
rules.whatItIs: Apps and runtimes installed system-wide with Flatpak.
rules.whyBig: Runtimes (GNOME, KDE, freedesktop, GPU drivers) are hundreds of MB each, and unused versions remain after updates.
rules.ifDeleted: Flatpak apps stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'flatpak uninstall --unused'.

rules.title: snapd data
rules.summary: Snap packages and snapd state; do not delete by hand
rules.whatItIs: State of the snap daemon and the snap package files (snaps) of every installed revision.
rules.whyBig: Each snap keeps several revisions (3 by default).
rules.ifDeleted: Every snap app (and on Ubuntu, parts of the system) stops working.
rules.saferAlternative: Lower kept revisions with 'sudo snap set system refresh.retain=2' and remove disabled revisions with 'snap remove <name> --revision=<rev>'.

rules.title: Snap package files
rules.summary: Snap packages, several revisions each; keep fewer revisions with snap set
rules.whatItIs: The compressed .snap files of every installed snap revision.
rules.whyBig: snapd keeps older revisions for rollback (3 by default), so each app can be counted two or three times.
rules.ifDeleted: Deleting files by hand breaks mounted snaps.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'sudo snap set system refresh.retain=2', then remove disabled revisions listed by 'snap list --all'.

rules.title: Snap mount points
rules.summary: Mounted snap packages; sizes here duplicate /var/lib/snapd/snaps
rules.whatItIs: Each installed snap revision is mounted here read-only from its .snap file.
rules.whyBig: These are mounted images, not extra data: the real files are in /var/lib/snapd/snaps, so scanning both counts them twice.
rules.ifDeleted: The files are read-only mounts and cannot be deleted; remove snaps with 'snap remove'.

rules.title: System programs (/usr)
rules.summary: Installed programs and libraries of the system; manage with your package manager
rules.whatItIs: Programs, libraries and shared data installed by the package manager.
rules.whyBig: Desktop environments, development tools, kernels' modules and big apps.
rules.ifDeleted: The system breaks; it may not boot.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove packages with your package manager (for example 'sudo apt autoremove').

rules.title: Boot files (/boot)
rules.summary: Kernels, initramfs and boot loader files
rules.whatItIs: Installed kernels, their initramfs images and the boot loader configuration.
rules.whyBig: Old kernels stay after upgrades and can fill a small /boot partition.
rules.ifDeleted: The system will not boot.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove old kernels with the package manager (for example 'sudo apt autoremove --purge').

rules.title: Optional software (/opt)
rules.summary: Third-party software installed outside the package manager
rules.whatItIs: Location for self-contained third-party software (browsers, IDEs, vendor tools).
rules.whyBig: Each application keeps its full installation here.
rules.ifDeleted: Those applications stop working.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall with the vendor's uninstaller or package.

rules.title: Temporary files (/tmp)
rules.summary: Temporary files; cleared at reboot on most systems
rules.whatItIs: Shared temporary folder; many distributions mount it in RAM (tmpfs) or clear it at boot.
rules.whyBig: Programs that crash or never clean up leave files behind.
rules.ifDeleted: Files of running programs (sockets, lock files, X11/Wayland session data) can break your session; old files are harmless to remove.
rules.saferAlternative: Reboot, or delete only old files you recognise.

rules.title: Persistent temporary files
rules.summary: Temporary files kept across reboots
rules.whatItIs: Temporary folder whose contents survive reboots; systemd usually removes files older than 30 days.
rules.whyBig: Large temporary files of build tools and installers.
rules.ifDeleted: Running programs may lose working files; old files are harmless to remove.

rules.title: Swap file
rules.summary: Swap space; turn it off before resizing or removing
rules.whatItIs: A file used as swap space (virtual memory).
rules.whyBig: Its size was chosen when it was created, often equal to RAM.
rules.ifDeleted: Deleting it while active is not possible; removing it without editing /etc/fstab causes boot delays or errors.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'sudo swapoff /swapfile', create a smaller one, and keep /etc/fstab consistent.

rules.title: lost+found
rules.summary: Recovered file fragments from fsck; the folder itself must exist
rules.whatItIs: Folder at the root of each ext file system where fsck puts recovered files.
rules.whyBig: Usually empty; after file system repairs it holds orphaned files.
rules.ifDeleted: The folder itself is needed by fsck; recovered files inside can be removed after checking them.

rules.title: /proc (virtual)
rules.summary: Virtual kernel file system; takes no disk space
rules.whatItIs: A virtual file system the kernel creates in memory with process and system information.
rules.whyBig: It uses no disk space; /proc/kcore shows the size of the address space (it can look like 128 TB) but is not stored anywhere.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing can be deleted here.

rules.title: /sys (virtual)
rules.summary: Virtual kernel file system for devices; takes no disk space
rules.whatItIs: A virtual file system with kernel and device information.
rules.whyBig: It uses no disk space.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing can be deleted here.

rules.title: /dev (devices)
rules.summary: Device files; takes no disk space
rules.whatItIs: Device nodes managed by the kernel and udev, held in memory.
rules.whyBig: It uses no disk space.
rules.ifDeleted: Deleting device nodes breaks access to hardware until reboot.
